examples.ko: 개가 죽은 날의 슬픔을 아직 못 잊었어요.
examples.en: I still haven't gotten over the sadness of the day my dog died.
My grandmother passed away, and my grief is still heavy.
If I write my sadness in a diary, my heart feels lighter.
I hugged my friend who was lost in sorrow.
To get over my sadness, I take a walk every morning.

explain: ‘슬프다’에 ‘-ㅁ’을 붙이면 ‘슬픔’이 돼요. ‘기쁘다’는 ‘기쁨’이 돼요. 이렇게 형용사를 명사로 바꿀 수 있어요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: He was steeped in sorrow and could not speak.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Jeongsun's voice trembled with resentment and sorrow.

explain_en: Add -ㅁ to 슬프다 and you get 슬픔; 기쁘다 becomes 기쁨. This is one way to turn an adjective into a noun.

examples.en: On our honeymoon we toured an old castle.
There's a big castle on the hill.
Long ago, a princess lived in a tall castle.
There is an old fortress in Suwon.

examples.ko: 성 위에서 뭐가 보여요? — 도시가 한눈에 보여요.
examples.en: What can you see from the castle wall? — I can see the whole city at a glance.

explain: 한국의 옛 ‘성’은 서양의 성처럼 큰 집이 아니라 도시를 둘러싼 긴 돌담인 경우가 많아요. 왕이 사는 곳은 ‘궁’이라고 해요.
explain_en: An old Korean 성 is often not a big house like a Western castle but a long stone wall around a town. Where the king lived is called 궁 (palace).

examples.en: Long ago, a king lived in this castle.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 옛날 왕이 쓴 모자를 봤어요.
examples.en: At the museum I saw a hat that a king wore long ago.

examples.ko: 옛날 이야기에서 왕은 늘 공주를 걱정해요.
examples.en: In old tales, the king always worries about the princess.

examples.ko: 한국에도 왕이 있어요? — 지금은 없어요. 옛날에는 있었어요.
examples.en: Does Korea have a king too? — Not now. It used to, long ago.
In chess, you win if you capture the king.

phrases.nuance_en: the prefix 왕- adds the sense of "very, extremely" to a word

dict_examples.en: When it comes to eating, I'm the king.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The lion is the king of animals.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 아파서 학교에 못 나오게 되기 전까지만 해도 그 아이는 학급에서 왕 노릇을 하였었다.
dict_examples.en: Until he got sick and couldn't come to school, that child ruled the class like a king.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: The king's wife is 왕비 (queen), his son is 왕자 (prince) and his daughter is 공주 (princess).

en: to build; to make up (a name)

examples.ko: 이 성은 옛날 왕이 지은 성이에요.
examples.en: This castle was built by a king long ago.
My grandfather chose my name.
I want to build a small house by the sea.
I want to build a small house in the countryside.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 십 년 전에 지었어요.
examples.en: This building was built ten years ago.

explain: ‘짓다’는 ㅅ이 사라져요: 지어요, 지었어요, 지은 집. 사전에 나오는 모양과 달라서 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 아이가 선물을 보고 환한 웃음을 지었어요.
phrases.en: to smile, to put on a smile
phrases.nuance_en: used when you form a smile on your face
phrases.en_equiv: to smile, to put on a smile

phrases.nuance_en: used for cooking rice, with a slightly old-fashioned, written feel

phrases.en: to have a prescription made up
phrases.nuance_en: used when a pharmacy prepares medicine according to a prescription
phrases.en_equiv: to have a prescription made up

explain_en: 짓다 drops its ㅅ before a vowel: 지어요, 지었어요, 지은 집. The conjugated form looks different from the dictionary form.

dis.h: everyday native verb: make a house

p.n: 건축하다 sounds more formal and technical than 짓다.

examples.en: The groom in the photo is my grandfather.
The groom sang a song at the wedding.
The groom wore a white suit.
The bride and groom cut the cake together.

examples.ko: 신랑이 누구예요? — 저기 파란 양복을 입은 사람이에요.
examples.en: Who is the groom? — The one over there in the blue suit.

explain: ‘신랑’은 결혼식 때 쓰는 말이에요. 결혼한 뒤에 남편을 부를 때나 말할 때는 ‘남편’이라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: to welcome the bridegroom
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to become a bridegroom
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 혼인날 신랑을 구경하려고 많은 마을 사람이 모여 들었다.
dict_examples.en: Many villagers gathered to see the bridegroom on the wedding day.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 신랑 is the word for the wedding day. Once married, he is called 남편 (husband).

examples.en: The bride in the photo is my grandmother.
The bride wore a white dress.
The bride walked in slowly, holding flowers.

examples.ko: 신부 가족과 신랑 가족이 같이 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The bride's family and the groom's family took a photo together.

examples.ko: 신부가 어디 있어요? — 저기 꽃 옆에 있어요.
examples.en: Where is the bride? — Over there next to the flowers.

explain: ‘신부’는 가톨릭 성당의 신부(priest)라는 뜻도 있어요. 소리는 같지만 한자와 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: 신부 also means a Catholic priest. The sound is the same, but the Chinese characters and the meaning are different.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 신혼여행으로 바닷가 마을에 갔어요.
examples.en: The two of them went to a seaside village for their honeymoon.
Where are you going for your honeymoon?
Many people go to Jeju Island for their honeymoon.
I hung the photos from our honeymoon in the living room.
I took time off work for my honeymoon.

explain: ‘신혼여행’은 ‘허니문’이라고도 해요. 여행사 광고에서 자주 볼 수 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: A honeymoon is also called ‘허니문’ (honeymoon). You often see it in travel agency ads.

examples.en: The show we saw yesterday was really fun.
After the show, we took photos with the actors.
There is a street performance this weekend.

examples.ko: 공연 표는 인터넷에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy performance tickets online.

examples.ko: 공연이 몇 시에 시작해요? — 저녁 일곱 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: What time does the show start? — It starts at seven in the evening.

explain: 콘서트, 뮤지컬, 연극, 춤 무대를 모두 ‘공연’이라고 불러요. 영화는 공연이 아니에요.
explain_en: Concerts, musicals, plays and dance shows are all called 공연. A movie is not a 공연.

examples.en: Last week I went to a photo exhibition with a friend.
I still think about a painting I saw at the exhibition.
Admission to this exhibition is free.

examples.ko: 전시회가 다음 달 십오 일까지 열려요.
examples.en: The exhibition is open until the fifteenth of next month.

examples.ko: 전시회에서 사진을 찍어도 돼요? — 아니요, 사진은 안 돼요.
examples.en: Can I take photos at the exhibition? — No, photos are not allowed.

explain: 박물관과 미술관은 건물이고, 전시회는 정해진 기간에만 하는 행사예요. 전시회는 미술관 안에서도 열려요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: A museum or gallery is a building; a 전시회 is an event that runs for a set period. An exhibition can be held inside a gallery.

en: to give back, to return (an item)

examples.en: I gave back the book I borrowed from my friend.

examples.ko: 친구가 빌려 간 돈을 아직 안 돌려줬어요.
examples.en: My friend still hasn't paid back the money he borrowed.
I'll give back the umbrella I borrowed tomorrow.
I'm going to return the laptop I borrowed from my friend.
The police gave back the wallet I had lost.

explain: 빌린 돈은 ‘갚다’도 써요. 도서관 책이나 영화 DVD는 ‘반납하다’를 많이 써요.

dict_examples.ko: 급해서 그러니 내게 이백만 원만 돌려주게.
dict_examples.en: I'm in a hurry, so please lend me just two million won.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: For borrowed money, 갚다 is also used. For library books or rented DVDs, 반납하다 is very common.

examples.en: I took a book out of my bag.
I took the milk out of the fridge.
I took my phone out of my pocket and took a photo.
I took my winter coat out of the closet.
Please take some ice out of the freezer.

explain: 꺼내는 곳에는 ‘에서’를 써요: 가방에서 꺼내요. 넣는 곳에는 ‘에’를 써요: 가방에 넣어요.

phrases.nuance_en: used when you start talking about something hard to bring up

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to take clothes out of the wardrobe
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 나는 안 호주머니에서 수첩을 꺼내고 그 속에 든 주민 등록증을 계장에게 넘겨주었다.
dict_examples.en: I took a notebook out of my inner pocket and handed the resident registration card inside to the section chief.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 계숙은 미리 준비하였던 과자와 과일을 꺼내 놓고 계속 권한다.
dict_examples.en: Gyesuk takes out the snacks and fruit she prepared earlier and keeps offering them.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: The place you take something out of takes 에서: 가방에서 꺼내요. The place you put it into takes 에: 가방에 넣어요.

dis.h: take an item out from inside

p.n: 빼다 sounds unnatural for taking a book out of a bag; it is for pulling out something fixed or stuck.

examples.en: I keep the letters my friends gave me in a box.
Keep leftovers in the fridge.
I keep important documents in a drawer.

examples.ko: 이 약은 시원한 곳에 보관해야 해요.
examples.en: This medicine has to be stored in a cool place.

examples.ko: 큰 가방은 어디에 보관해요? — 호텔 방에 두어요.
examples.en: Where do you keep your big suitcase? — I leave it in the hotel room.

explain: ‘보관하다’는 물건을 잃어버리지 않게 잘 두는 거예요. 다른 사람에게 내 물건을 잠깐 부탁할 때는 ‘맡기다’를 써요: 호텔에 짐을 맡겼어요. 말할 때는 ‘넣어 두다’, ‘잘 둬요’도 많이 써요.

dict_examples.en: to keep photos in an album
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: He keeps the jewelry in a safe.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 보관하다 means keeping something safe so it doesn't get lost. When you hand your things to someone else to look after, use 맡기다: 'I left my luggage at the hotel.' In everyday talk, 넣어 두다 and 잘 둬요 are also common.

p.n: 간직하다 makes the photos sound treasured, not just stored.

examples.en: I put the photos from the trip in a photo album.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 사진첩에 고양이 사진이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: My phone's photo gallery is full of cat pictures.
I found an old photo album at my grandmother's house.

examples.ko: 사진첩을 보니까 어릴 때 생각이 나요.
examples.en: Looking at the album reminds me of my childhood.

examples.ko: 사진첩에 누구 사진이 있어요? — 가족 사진하고 친구 사진이 있어요.
examples.en: Whose photos are in the album? — Family photos and friends' photos.

explain_en: On a phone, the photo app is often called 갤러리 or 앨범. Printed photos go in a 사진첩 or 앨범.

examples.ko: 이 책 표지에는 바다 사진이 있어요.
examples.en: This book's cover has a photo of the sea on it.
I bought the book because the cover was pretty.

examples.ko: 이 잡지 표지에 나온 가수를 어제 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the singer from this magazine cover yesterday.

examples.ko: 표지만 보고 책을 고르면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't choose a book just by its cover.
I wrote my name on the cover of my notebook.

explain: 책의 맨 앞 겉장은 ‘앞표지’, 맨 뒤 겉장은 ‘뒤표지’라고 해요.
explain_en: The very front cover is 앞표지 and the back cover is 뒤표지.
